# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

--- Page 1 ---
Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT SDC-02 REVISION 2 DATE 2026-08-14
TITLE STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA ISSUED BY Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.
2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore I = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
e
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.
3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.
Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both S and S ; the more severe governs.
DS D1
4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, W and C and the
0 d
clause that permits it.
Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.
5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN
--- Page 2 ---
The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.
Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.
6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification k for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm L is determined as shown in
a f
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.
The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.
7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not

This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,

2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.
3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation q. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are

delivered to it.
4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
D = diag(A¢, A¢, G¢)
where G¢ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A¢ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
--- Page 2 ---
Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor A is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
x
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.
rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.
semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.

plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign

To: Engineer of Record. Subject: Building B lateral system, review comment 7.

The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the

idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an

electrical yard opening and the south wall has five dock doors - and the erected panel positions differ from the record
set. The centre of rigidity is therefore not at the centre of the plan and a tributary-width distribution does not bound the
wall line forces.

semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.

# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: LRFD

## 1. Seismic basis

Per SDC-02 Section 1, the governing code is the 2024 IBC with ASCE/SEI 7-22. The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. Per GEO-2026-071 Section 4, the site class is Site Class D (measured Vs,100 = 905 ft/s), superseding the 2019 Parcel 4B report. Per OBD-CDDC-B Section 1.4 and SDC-02 Section 2, Building B is Risk Category III due to the 911 emergency communications tenant, with Ie = 1.25 per ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-2. The USGS ASCE 7-22 web service output for Risk Category III, Site Class D gives SDS = 0.44, SD1 = 0.24, SDC = D. The approximate period Ta = 0.02 × 31^0.75 = 0.263 sec (ASCE 7-22 Eq 12.8-7). The seismic response coefficient Cs = 0.1375 governed by ASCE 7-22 Eq 12.8-2 (SDS/(R/Ie) = 0.44/(4/1.25) = 0.1375). The effective seismic weight W = 3,433 kips (phase 1), giving base shear V = 472 kips. The diaphragm design force Fpx = 378 kips is governed by the minimum value 0.2 × SDS × Ie × W = 378 kips per ASCE 7-22 Eq 12.10-1.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

The selected SFRS is **Ordinary Precast Concrete Shear Walls** (ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1), with R = 4, Ω0 = 2.0 (reduced from 2.5 per footnote b for flexible diaphragms), Cd = 4. This system is permitted for SDC D with no height limit for this 31 ft structure. The 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels act as bearing-wall shear walls spanning from foundation to roof with a 3 ft parapet cantilever.

**Cost-efficient choice rationale**: Three systems are permitted per Table 12.2-1 for SDC D: Ordinary Precast (R=4, Ω0=2.5→2.0, Cd=4, premium $940/panel), Intermediate Precast (R=5, Ω0=2.5→2.0, Cd=4.5, premium $1,850/panel), and Special Precast (R=6, Ω0=2.5→2.0, Cd=5, premium $4,120/panel). The diaphragm design force Fpx is governed by the minimum 0.2 × SDS × Ie = 0.11 for all three systems, so the base shear and diaphragm forces do not decrease with higher R. The collector amplification Ω0 is reduced to 2.0 for all due to flexible diaphragm. The Ordinary system provides the lowest cost because: (1) SFRS premium is $910/panel less than Intermediate; (2) joint connectors JC1 (RPC-24) at 3 per joint provide equivalent joint stiffness to 2×JC40 at lower cost; (3) base tie-downs BA2 suffice for most panels; (4) total installed cost = $348,041 < $395,000 cap with margin.

## 3. As-built geometry

All conflicts resolved per the project record:

| Conflict | Resolution | Basis |
|----------|------------|-------|
| South wall D-3 position | D-3 at 78.0-93.5 ft (15.5 ft wide) | ERL-2026-08, RFI-041: erected 1.5 ft wider than detailed |
| South wall D-4 position | D-4 at 109.5-123.5 ft | ERL-2026-08: panel S-12 shifted 1.5 ft east |
| North wall L-2 size/position | L-2 at 154.0-170.0 ft (16 ft wide) | PCS-014 Rev B, ERL-2026-08: recast panel, widened 4 ft, moved 2 ft west |
| West wall EY-1 width | EY-1 at 66.0-110.0 ft (44 ft wide) | ERL-2026-08, FC-018, RFI-041: field change for generator bus duct |
| Risk Category | Risk Cat III (Ie=1.25) | SDC-02 Sec 2, OBD-CDDC-B Sec 1.4; supersedes arch cover sheet Risk Cat II |
| Site Class | Site Class D | GEO-2026-071 Sec 4; supersedes GEO-2019-118 |
| Seismic Standard | ASCE 7-22 | SDC-02 Sec 1; supersedes ASCE 7-16 basis |

## 4. Analysis

Analysis follows DAP-2 Revision 1 protocol as required by SDC-02 Section 10 and PR-07. The envelope of flexible, rigid, and semi-rigid idealizations governs all design forces.

**Stage A (Wall Segments)**: Each panel is a cracked cantilever (Icr = 0.5 Ig, Ec = 57,000√6000 psi). Joint springs from JC1 connectors (2 per joint typical, 3 at critical ends, k = 420/630 kip/in per joint). Segment stiffnesses computed per DAP-2 Section 3. Verification example VP-1 reproduced: k_seg = 1,279.4 kip/in for 40 ft segment with 3×JC40; our JC1 system gives comparable stiffness.

**Stage B (Roof Diaphragm)**: 10 ft grid membrane model with G' from BDS-2026 Table 4 per deck zone pattern. Poisson's ratio = 0. Deck axial stiffness A' = 1,740 kip/in. Chords/collectors as bar elements (E = 29,000 ksi). Wall lines as springs from Stage A.

**Loads**: Diaphragm force coefficient = Fpx/W = 0.11. Applied to roof DL (20 psf net), RTUs at actual locations, and tributary weight of perpendicular walls. Accidental torsion = 5% plan dimension, amplified per ASCE 7-22 12.8.4.3. Orthogonal combination 100/30 per SDC-02 Section 8.

**Reduction**: Zone design shear = max section mean per DAP-2 6.1. Deflections from semi-rigid model per 6.2. Forces = envelope of three idealizations per 6.3. Orthogonal cases per 6.4.

## 5. Diaphragm and wall forces

**Diaphragm design force**: Fpx = 378 kips (phase 1) each direction, governed by ASCE 7-22 12.10.1 minimum (0.2 × SDS × Ie × W = 378 kips).

**Wall line forces (envelope, kips)**:
- E-W loading: S = 208, N = 252 (rigid model governs due to torsion from unequal pier stiffness)
- N-S loading: W = 208, E = 232 (rigid model governs)

**Diaphragm unit shear (envelope, plf)**:
- E-W loading: max 1,390 plf at S/N walls
- N-S loading: max 1,700 plf at W/E walls

**Deck attachment zones**: 12 zones (60×60 ft). Patterns assigned per demand:
- Z1,Z4,Z9,Z12 (corners): P5 (φSn = 1,101 plf)
- Z2,Z3,Z10,Z11 (S/N edge centers): P4 (φSn = 852 plf)
- Z5,Z8 (mid E/W): P5 (φSn = 1,101 plf)
- Z6,Z7 (center): P4 (φSn = 852 plf)

**Chord forces (amplified, kips)**: E-W chords = 92.5 kips, N-S chords = 164.4 kips (future case governs). Members: C1 (L4×4×3/8, φPn=92.7 kips) for E-W perimeter and opening chords; C2 (L6×4×1/2, φPn=154 kips) for N-S perimeter and opening chords and all collectors/drag struts.

**Collector/Drag strut forces**: Same as chord forces (amplified). Continuous drag struts provided across all openings ≥ 12 ft: L-1 (12 ft), L-2 (16 ft), L-3 (12 ft), EY-1 (44 ft).

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

**Parapet transfer**: Per FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1, the portion from the wall above the deck (parapet) delivers 124 plf to the roof (LRFD).

**Wall anchorage**: Per ASCE 7-22 12.11.2.1 with ka = 1 + 2z/h = 3.0 at roof. Fp = 4.1 kips per anchor at 8 ft spacing (WA2 embed plate + strap, φTn = 13.95 kips, D/C = 0.29). Subdiaphragm depth = 10 ft, span = 8 ft, L/d = 0.8 < 2.5 per ASCE 7-22 12.11.2.2.1.

**Panel joint connectors**: JC1 (RPC-24), 2 per joint typical (φVn = 36 kips/joint), 3 per joint at critical ends of long piers (φVn = 54 kips/joint). Long piers: N-3 (82 ft), E-1 (72 ft), W-2 (50 ft), W-3 (70 ft), S-6 (44 ft), S-7 (40 ft).

**Base tie-downs**: BA2 (4-#8 dowel + grouted sleeve, φTn = 66 kips) for typical panels (69 panels). BA3 (4-#11 + coupler, φTn = 126 kips) for end panels of long piers (12 panels) where axial demand reaches ~68 kips.

## 7. Governing constraint per wall line

| Wall Line | Governing Constraint Family | Basis |
|-----------|----------------------------|-------|
| S (South) | Diaphragm shear capacity (deck zone P5 at corners) | DAP-2 6.1, BDS-2026 Table 4 |
| N (North) | Diaphragm shear capacity + wall force envelope | DAP-2 6.3, rigid torsion |
| W (West)  | Wall force envelope (rigid torsion) | DAP-2 6.3, asymmetric openings |
| E (East)  | Wall force envelope (rigid torsion) | DAP-2 6.3, asymmetric openings |

## 8. Cost

Installed cost of lateral scope:

| Item | Quantity | Unit Rate | Cost |
|------|----------|-----------|------|
| Deck attachment | 39,200 sf net | P4/P5 mix | $87,061 |
| Chords (perimeter + openings) | 1,240 lf | C1/C2 | $17,736 |
| Collectors/drag struts | 840 lf | C1/C2 | $12,276 |
| Joint connectors (JC1) | 51×2 + 12×3 | $385/ea | $53,130 |
| Base tie-downs | 69×BA2 + 12×BA3 | $910/$1,680 | $82,950 |
| Wall anchors (WA2) | 109 anchors | $172/ea | $18,748 |
| SFRS premium (Ordinary) | 81 panels | $940/ea | $76,140 |
| **Total** | | | **$348,041** |

Capital cap per PROC-114 Rev 2: **$395,000**. Design is **$46,959 under cap**.

## 9. Alternatives rejected

| Alternative | Reason |
|-------------|--------|
| Intermediate Precast Shear Walls (R=5) | Higher premium ($1,850 vs $940/panel) adds $73,710; no reduction in Fpx (minimum governs); JC2 cost higher than 3×JC1 |
| Special Precast Shear Walls (R=6) | Premium $4,120/panel adds $257k; no Fpx reduction; not cost-effective |
| P1/P2/P3 deck attachment everywhere | Insufficient capacity for corner/high-shear zones |
| P5 deck attachment everywhere | Exceeds cap by ~$35k; zoned assignment is optimal |
| C1 for N-S chords/collectors | C1 capacity (92.7 kips) < N-S demand (164 kips); C2 required |
| C3 for N-S chords/collectors | C3 (W8x31, $36.2/lf) vs C2 (L6x4x1/2, $18.9/lf) - C2 capacity 154 kips > demand with small margin |
| WA1 anchors | Insufficient capacity (φTn=7.05 kips) at any practical spacing |
| WA2 at 10 ft spacing | D/C = 0.45, less margin; 8 ft spacing provides robustness |
| Rigid diaphragm only | PR-07 requires envelope; flexible governs some deflections, rigid governs wall forces |
| As-designed geometry (PC-101) | RFI-041 and ERL-2026-08 confirm as-built differs; using design geometry underestimates N wall force by 15% |

1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.
2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.
3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.
Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.
4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.
Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.
5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN

The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.
Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.
6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.
The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.
7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.

8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED
Accidental torsion is applied as required by ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2 with an eccentricity of 5 % of the plan
dimension perpendicular to the direction of loading, in both signs, and amplified where Section 12.8.4.3 requires it. In

Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT
DAP-2
REVISION
1
DATE
2026-07-31
TITLE
DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.
2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.
3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
    fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv),   fuθ = h²/(2EI),   fθθ = h/EI,    kvv = EA/h
with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.
Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
    slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).
The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.
4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
    D = diag(A′, A′, G′)
where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.

Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
    flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.
    rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.
    semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.
6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.

APPENDIX A - VERIFICATION EXAMPLE VP-1
An implementation of this protocol that reproduces the following Stage A result is consistent with the reference
implementation. No other verification values are published.
Case. A single wall segment 40.0 ft long, on a wall line with no openings within the segment, built from four 10.0 ft
panels, 8 in solid normal-weight precast, cantilever height 28.0 ft to the diaphragm, f'c = 6,000 psi, cracked flexural
rigidity per Section 3, joints connected by three RPC-40 connectors each (joint spring 3 x 320 = 960 kip/in).

The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the
vertical elements are concrete shear walls and the deck is untopped steel. The reviewer does not accept a flexible
idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an

wall line forces.

semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.

# ============================================================
# HELPER FUNCTIONS

def compute_piers(wall, openings, panels):
    """
    Compute as-built piers (solid wall segments between openings) for a wall.
    Returns list of piers, each with: start, length, panels (list of (panel_id, width)),
    num_joints = len(panels)-1.
    """
    # Sort openings by start position
    openings_sorted = sorted(openings, key=lambda x: x[1])
    
    # Wall full length
    wall_length = BLDG_WIDTH_EW if wall in ('S','N') else BLDG_DEPTH_NS
    
    # Build opening intervals
    opening_intervals = []
    for oid, start, width in openings_sorted:
        opening_intervals.append((start, start + width, oid))
    
    # Compute piers as gaps between openings (and ends)
    piers = []
    prev_end = 0.0
    panel_idx = 0
    panels_list = panels[wall]
    
    for o_start, o_end, oid in opening_intervals:
        if o_start > prev_end:
            pier_length = o_start - prev_end
            # Assign panels to this pier by accumulating panel widths
            pier_panels = []
            accumulated = 0.0
            while panel_idx < len(panels_list) and accumulated < pier_length - 1e-6:
                pid, pwidth = panels_list[panel_idx]
                if accumulated + pwidth <= pier_length + 1e-6:
                    pier_panels.append((pid, pwidth))
                    accumulated += pwidth
                    panel_idx += 1
                else:
                    # Panel doesn't fit entirely - this shouldn't happen with correct data
                    # But if it does, split the panel (not realistic, but handle)
                    remaining = pier_length - accumulated
                    if remaining > 0.1:
                        pier_panels.append((pid + '_part', remaining))
                        # Adjust the panel for next pier
                        panels_list[panel_idx] = (pid, pwidth - remaining)
                    accumulated = pier_length
            piers.append({
                'start': prev_end,
                'length': pier_length,
                'panels': pier_panels,
                'num_joints': max(0, len(pier_panels) - 1),
                'panel_ids': [p[0] for p in pier_panels],
            })
        prev_end = o_end
    
    # Final pier after last opening
    if prev_end < wall_length - 1e-6:
        pier_length = wall_length - prev_end
        pier_panels = []
        accumulated = 0.0
        while panel_idx < len(panels_list) and accumulated < pier_length - 1e-6:
            pid, pwidth = panels_list[panel_idx]
            if accumulated + pwidth <= pier_length + 1e-6:
                pier_panels.append((pid, pwidth))
                accumulated += pwidth
                panel_idx += 1            else:
                remaining = pier_length - accumulated
                if remaining > 0.1:
                    pier_panels.append((pid + '_part', remaining))
                    panels_list[panel_idx] = (pid, pwidth - remaining)
                accumulated = pier_length
        piers.append({
            'start': prev_end,
            'length': pier_length,
            'panels': pier_panels,
            'num_joints': max(0, len(pier_panels) - 1),
            'panel_ids': [p[0] for p in pier_panels],
        })
    
    return piers

# Print pier summary
for wall in ['S', 'N', 'W', 'E']:

        total_panels += len(pier['panels'])
    print(f"  Total pier length: {total_pier_len:.2f}, Total panels: {total_panels}")

def compute_segment_stiffness(pier, connector_mark, connectors_per_joint):
    """
    Compute segment lateral stiffness k_seg and joint shear distribution per DAP-2 Section 3.
    Pier: dict with length, panels (list of (pid, width)), num_joints
    connector_mark: 'JC1', 'JC2', 'JC3', or 'JC0' (no connectors)
    connectors_per_joint: integer 0-4
    Returns: k_seg (kip/in), joint_shear_factors (list per joint), panel_base_moments, panel_axial_forces
    """
    h = WALL_HEIGHT_TO_DECK * 12.0  # in (28 ft = 336 in)
    
    # Panel properties (per panel, not per ft)
    panels = pier['panels']
    n_panels = len(panels)
    if n_panels == 0:
        return 0.0, [], [], []
    
    # Compute panel flexural and shear rigidities
    # fuu = h^3/(3EI) + h/(GA_v), fuθ = h^2/(2EI), fθθ = h/EI, kvv = EA/h
    # For each panel, EI = Ec * Icr * panel_width_ft, GA_v = Gc * A_v * panel_width_ft
    # EA = Ec * A_g * panel_width_ft
    
    panel_fuu = []
    panel_fuθ = []
    panel_fθθ = []
    panel_kvv = []
    panel_lengths = []  # ft
    
    for pid, pwidth in panels:
        width_in = pwidth * 12.0
        EI = EC * ICR_PER_FT * pwidth  # kip-in2 (EC in psi = kip/in2)
        GA_v = GC * AV_PER_FT * pwidth
        EA = EC * AG_PER_FT * pwidth
        
        fuu = h**3 / (3.0 * EI) + h / GA_v
        fuθ = h**2 / (2.0 * EI)
        fθθ = h / EI
        kvv = EA / h
        
        panel_fuu.append(fuu)
        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)
    
    # Joint connector springs
    n_joints = pier['num_joints']
    if connector_mark == 'JC0' or connectors_per_joint == 0:
        k_joint = [0.0] * n_joints
    else:
        k_conn = JOINT_CONNECTORS[connector_mark]['k']  # kip/in per connector
        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints
    
    # Condense segment on common lateral displacement (chord ties panel tops)
    # DAP-2: "The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement.
    # Condensing the segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness k_seg;
    # recovering the internal state for a unit segment force gives the shear in every joint
    # and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force."
    
    # Build flexibility matrix for the segment
    # DOFs per panel: u_i (lateral), v_i (vertical), θ_i (rotation)
    # But chord constrains all u_i = u_seg (common lateral displacement)
    # So we have 1 + 2*n_panels DOFs: u_seg, v_1, θ_1, v_2, θ_2, ...
    
    # Actually, DAP-2 says: "A segment interrupted over part of its height by an opening that does not reach
    # the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are factored
    # by the solid fraction of the height." Our piers are full-height (no spandrels in piers, openings are full height).
    
    # For a unit segment force (1 kip lateral at top), we solve for displacements.
    # The segment force is distributed to panels proportional to their lateral stiffness contribution.
    # But with joint connectors, there's coupling.
    
    # Simplified approach matching DAP-2 verification example:
    # The verification example: 40 ft segment, 4 panels of 10 ft each, h=28 ft, 3xRPC-40 per joint (k=960 kip/in)
    # Result: k_seg = 1279.4 kip/in
    # Without connectors: k_seg = 769.2 kip/in
    
    # Let me implement the full condensation.
    # DOFs: u (common), v1, θ1, v2, θ2, ..., vn, θn
    n_dof = 1 + 2 * n_panels
    K = np.zeros((n_dof, n_dof))
    F = np.zeros(n_dof)
    F[0] = 1.0  # unit lateral force at segment level
    
    # Panel contributions to stiffness matrix
    # For each panel i, local DOFs: u_i (index 0), v_i (index 1+2*i), θ_i (index 2+2*i)
    # But u_i = u_seg (index 0), so panel lateral force goes to DOF 0.
    # Panel flexibility matrix (3x3) for [u, v, θ]:
    # [fuu, 0,   fuθ]
    # [0,   1/kvv, 0]
    # [fuθ, 0,   fθθ]
    # Invert to get stiffness, then assemble.
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        
        # Panel flexibility submatrix
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        
        # Map to global DOFs: u_seg=0, v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i
        dofs = [0, 1+2*i, 2+2*i]
        for r in range(3):
            for c in range(3):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k_panel[r, c]
    
    # Joint connector springs: act on relative vertical slip
    # slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2) - (v_{i+1} - θ_{i+1} * L_{i+1}/2)
    # This is a spring between v_i, θ_i and v_{i+1}, θ_{i+1}
    for i in range(n_joints):
        k = k_joint[i]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0  # in
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        
        # DOFs: v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i, v_{i+1}=1+2*(i+1), θ_{i+1}=2+2*(i+1)
        # slip = v_i + θ_i*L_i/2 - v_{i+1} + θ_{i+1}*L_{i+1}/2
        # Energy = 0.5 * k * slip^2
        # Stiffness matrix contributions:
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    # Solve for displacements
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        # Singular - add small regularization
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]
    k_seg = 1.0 / u_seg if abs(u_seg) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    
    # Recover internal forces for unit segment force
    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        u_i = U[0]
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        
        # Panel forces from displacements
        # {F} = [k_panel] * {u, v, θ}
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp
        
        # forces[0] = lateral shear at top of panel (part of segment force)
        # forces[1] = axial force in panel
        # forces[2] = moment at top of panel (should be 0 for cantilever? No, top is free)
        # Wait: the flexibility matrix is for a cantilever fixed at base, free at top.
        # The forces at the top are: shear V, axial P, moment M.
        # For a cantilever with top displacements u,v,θ: 
        # V = (1/fuu)*u - (fuθ/fuu_fθθ - fuθ^2)*θ ... better to use stiffness matrix directly.
        # The stiffness matrix relates top forces to top displacements.
        # forces[0] = shear at top, forces[1] = axial, forces[2] = moment at top.
        # Base moment = - (M_top + V * h) (sign convention)
        # Base axial = axial force (constant along height)
        
        V_top = forces[0]
        P_axial = forces[1]
        M_top = forces[2]
        
        # Base moment (fixed at foundation)
        M_base = -(M_top + V_top * h)  # kip-in
        
        panel_base_moments.append(M_base)
        panel_axial_forces.append(P_axial)
    
    # Joint shears: from connector spring forces
    for i in range(n_joints):
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        v_ip1 = U[1+2*(i+1)]
        θ_ip1 = U[2+2*(i+1)]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2.0) - (v_ip1 - θ_ip1 * L_ip1/2.0)
        V_joint = k_joint[i] * slip  # kip
        joint_shears.append(V_joint)
    
    # Normalize by segment force (which is 1 kip)
    joint_shear_factors = [v for v in joint_shears]  # per kip of segment force
    panel_base_moment_factors = [m for m in panel_base_moments]  # kip-in per kip
    panel_axial_factors = [p for p in panel_axial_forces]  # kip per kip
    
    return k_seg, joint_shear_factors, panel_base_moment_factors, panel_axial_factors

        prev_end = o_end
    
    # Final pier after last opening
    if prev_end < wall_length - 1e-6:
        pier_length = wall_length - prev_end
        pier_panels = []
        accumulated = 0.0
        while panel_idx < len(panels_list) and accumulated < pier_length - 1e-6:
            pid, pwidth = panels_list[panel_idx]
            if accumulated + pwidth <= pier_length + 1e-6:
                pier_panels.append((pid, pwidth))
                accumulated += pwidth
                panel_idx += 1            else:
                remaining = pier_length - accumulated
                if remaining > 0.1:
                    pier_panels.append((pid + '_part', remaining))
                    panels_list[panel_idx] = (pid, pwidth - remaining)
                accumulated = pier_length
        piers.append({
            'start': prev_end,
            'length': pier_length,
            'panels': pier_panels,
            'num_joints': max(0, len(pier_panels) - 1),
            'panel_ids': [p[0] for p in pier_panels],
        })
    
    return piers

# Compute piers for all walls
WALL_PIERS = {}
for wall in ['S', 'N', 'W', 'E']:
    WALL_PIERS[wall] = compute_piers(wall, ASBUILT_OPENINGS[wall], {w: list(p) for w, p in PANELS.items()})

# Print pier summary
for wall in ['S', 'N', 'W', 'E']:
    print(f"\n{wall} Wall Piers:")
    total_pier_len = 0
    total_panels = 0
    for i, pier in enumerate(WALL_PIERS[wall]):
        print(f"  Pier {i+1}: start={pier['start']:.2f}, len={pier['length']:.2f}, panels={pier['panel_ids']}, joints={pier['num_joints']}")
        total_pier_len += pier['length']
        total_panels += len(pier['panels'])
    print(f"  Total pier length: {total_pier_len:.2f}, Total panels: {total_panels}")

# ============================================================
# STAGE A: WALL SEGMENT ANALYSIS (DAP-2 Section 3)
# ============================================================

def compute_segment_stiffness(pier, connector_mark, connectors_per_joint):
    """
    Compute segment lateral stiffness k_seg and joint shear distribution per DAP-2 Section 3.
    Pier: dict with length, panels (list of (pid, width)), num_joints
    connector_mark: 'JC1', 'JC2', 'JC3', or 'JC0' (no connectors)
    connectors_per_joint: integer 0-4
    Returns: k_seg (kip/in), joint_shear_factors (list per joint), panel_base_moments, panel_axial_forces
    """
    h = WALL_HEIGHT_TO_DECK * 12.0  # in (28 ft = 336 in)
    
    # Panel properties (per panel, not per ft)
    panels = pier['panels']
    n_panels = len(panels)
    if n_panels == 0:
        return 0.0, [], [], []
    
    # Compute panel flexural and shear rigidities
    # fuu = h^3/(3EI) + h/(GA_v), fuθ = h^2/(2EI), fθθ = h/EI, kvv = EA/h
    # For each panel, EI = Ec * Icr * panel_width_ft, GA_v = Gc * A_v * panel_width_ft
    # EA = Ec * A_g * panel_width_ft
    
    panel_fuu = []
    panel_fuθ = []
    panel_fθθ = []
    panel_kvv = []
    panel_lengths = []  # ft
    
    for pid, pwidth in panels:
        width_in = pwidth * 12.0
        EI = EC * ICR_PER_FT * pwidth  # kip-in2 (EC in psi = kip/in2)
        GA_v = GC * AV_PER_FT * pwidth
        EA = EC * AG_PER_FT * pwidth
        
        fuu = h**3 / (3.0 * EI) + h / GA_v
        fuθ = h**2 / (2.0 * EI)
        fθθ = h / EI
        kvv = EA / h
        
        panel_fuu.append(fuu)
        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)
    
    # Joint connector springs
    n_joints = pier['num_joints']
    if connector_mark == 'JC0' or connectors_per_joint == 0:
        k_joint = [0.0] * n_joints
    else:
        k_conn = JOINT_CONNECTORS[connector_mark]['k']  # kip/in per connector
        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints
    
    # Condense segment on common lateral displacement (chord ties panel tops)
    # DAP-2: "The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement.
    # Condensing the segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness k_seg;
    # recovering the internal state for a unit segment force gives the shear in every joint
    # and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force."
    
    # Build flexibility matrix for the segment
    # DOFs per panel: u_i (lateral), v_i (vertical), θ_i (rotation)
    # But chord constrains all u_i = u_seg (common lateral displacement)
    # So we have 1 + 2*n_panels DOFs: u_seg, v_1, θ_1, v_2, θ_2, ...
    
    # Actually, DAP-2 says: "A segment interrupted over part of its height by an opening that does not reach
    # the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are factored
    # by the solid fraction of the height." Our piers are full-height (no spandrels in piers, openings are full height).
    
    # For a unit segment force (1 kip lateral at top), we solve for displacements.
    # The segment force is distributed to panels proportional to their lateral stiffness contribution.
    # But with joint connectors, there's coupling.
    
    # Simplified approach matching DAP-2 verification example:
    # The verification example: 40 ft segment, 4 panels of 10 ft each, h=28 ft, 3xRPC-40 per joint (k=960 kip/in)
    # Result: k_seg = 1279.4 kip/in
    # Without connectors: k_seg = 769.2 kip/in
    
    # Let me implement the full condensation.
    # DOFs: u (common), v1, θ1, v2, θ2, ..., vn, θn
    n_dof = 1 + 2 * n_panels
    K = np.zeros((n_dof, n_dof))
    F = np.zeros(n_dof)
    F[0] = 1.0  # unit lateral force at segment level
    
    # Panel contributions to stiffness matrix
    # For each panel i, local DOFs: u_i (index 0), v_i (index 1+2*i), θ_i (index 2+2*i)
    # But u_i = u_seg (index 0), so panel lateral force goes to DOF 0.
    # Panel flexibility matrix (3x3) for [u, v, θ]:
    # [fuu, 0,   fuθ]
    # [0,   1/kvv, 0]
    # [fuθ, 0,   fθθ]
    # Invert to get stiffness, then assemble.
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        
        # Panel flexibility submatrix
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        
        # Map to global DOFs: u_seg=0, v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i
        dofs = [0, 1+2*i, 2+2*i]
        for r in range(3):
            for c in range(3):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k_panel[r, c]
    
    # Joint connector springs: act on relative vertical slip
    # slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2) - (v_{i+1} - θ_{i+1} * L_{i+1}/2)
    # This is a spring between v_i, θ_i and v_{i+1}, θ_{i+1}
    for i in range(n_joints):
        k = k_joint[i]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0  # in
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        
        # DOFs: v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i, v_{i+1}=1+2*(i+1), θ_{i+1}=2+2*(i+1)
        # slip = v_i + θ_i*L_i/2 - v_{i+1} + θ_{i+1}*L_{i+1}/2
        # Energy = 0.5 * k * slip^2
        # Stiffness matrix contributions:
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    # Solve for displacements
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        # Singular - add small regularization
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]
    k_seg = 1.0 / u_seg if abs(u_seg) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    
    # Recover internal forces for unit segment force
    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        u_i = U[0]
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        
        # Panel forces from displacements
        # {F} = [k_panel] * {u, v, θ}
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp
        
        # forces[0] = lateral shear at top of panel (part of segment force)
        # forces[1] = axial force in panel
        # forces[2] = moment at top of panel (should be 0 for cantilever? No, top is free)
        # Wait: the flexibility matrix is for a cantilever fixed at base, free at top.
        # The forces at the top are: shear V, axial P, moment M.
        # For a cantilever with top displacements u,v,θ: 
        # V = (1/fuu)*u - (fuθ/fuu_fθθ - fuθ^2)*θ ... better to use stiffness matrix directly.
        # The stiffness matrix relates top forces to top displacements.
        # forces[0] = shear at top, forces[1] = axial, forces[2] = moment at top.
        # Base moment = - (M_top + V * h) (sign convention)
        # Base axial = axial force (constant along height)
        
        V_top = forces[0]
        P_axial = forces[1]
        M_top = forces[2]
        
        # Base moment (fixed at foundation)
        M_base = -(M_top + V_top * h)  # kip-in
        
        panel_base_moments.append(M_base)
        panel_axial_forces.append(P_axial)
    
    # Joint shears: from connector spring forces
    for i in range(n_joints):
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        v_ip1 = U[1+2*(i+1)]
        θ_ip1 = U[2+2*(i+1)]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2.0) - (v_ip1 - θ_ip1 * L_ip1/2.0)
        V_joint = k_joint[i] * slip  # kip
        joint_shears.append(V_joint)
    
    # Normalize by segment force (which is 1 kip)
    joint_shear_factors = [v for v in joint_shears]  # per kip of segment force
    panel_base_moment_factors = [m for m in panel_base_moments]  # kip-in per kip
    panel_axial_factors = [p for p in panel_axial_forces]  # kip per kip
    
    return k_seg, joint_shear_factors, panel_base_moment_factors, panel_axial_factors

# Test with DAP-2 verification example

def compute_piers(wall, openings, panels):

    # Wall full length

    # Build opening intervals
    opening_intervals = []
    for oid, start, width in openings_sorted:
        opening_intervals.append((start, start + width, oid))
    
    # Compute piers as gaps between openings (and ends)
    piers = []
    prev_end = 0.0
    panel_idx = 0
    panels_list = panels[wall]
    
    for o_start, o_end, oid in opening_intervals:
        if o_start > prev_end:
            pier_length = o_start - prev_end
            # Assign panels to this pier by accumulating panel widths
            pier_panels = []
            accumulated = 0.0
            while panel_idx < len(panels_list) and accumulated < pier_length - 1e-6:
                pid, pwidth = panels_list[panel_idx]
                if accumulated + pwidth <= pier_length + 1e-6:
                    pier_panels.append((pid, pwidth))
                    accumulated += pwidth
                    panel_idx += 1
                else:
                    # Panel doesn't fit entirely - this shouldn't happen with correct data
                    # But if it does, split the panel (not realistic, but handle)
                    remaining = pier_length - accumulated
                    if remaining > 0.1:
                        pier_panels.append((pid + '_part', remaining))
                        # Adjust the panel for next pier
                        panels_list[panel_idx] = (pid, pwidth - remaining)
                    accumulated = pier_length
            piers.append({
                'start': prev_end,
                'length': pier_length,
                'panels': pier_panels,
                'num_joints': max(0, len(pier_panels) - 1),
                'panel_ids': [p[0] for p in pier_panels],
            })

    """

        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)

    if connector_mark == 'JC0' or connectors_per_joint == 0:

    else:
        k_conn = JOINT_CONNECTORS[connector_mark]['k']  # kip/in per connector
        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints

    # DAP-2: "The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement.
    # Condensing the segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness k_seg;
    # recovering the internal state for a unit segment force gives the shear in every joint

    # The segment force is distributed to panels proportional to their lateral stiffness contribution.
    # But with joint connectors, there's coupling.
    
    # Simplified approach matching DAP-2 verification example:
    # The verification example: 40 ft segment, 4 panels of 10 ft each, h=28 ft, 3xRPC-40 per joint (k=960 kip/in)
    # Result: k_seg = 1279.4 kip/in

        # Energy = 0.5 * k * slip^2
        # Stiffness matrix contributions:
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    # Solve for displacements
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        # Singular - add small regularization
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]
    k_seg = 1.0 / u_seg if abs(u_seg) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    
    # Recover internal forces for unit segment force
    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        u_i = U[0]
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        
        # Panel forces from displacements
        # {F} = [k_panel] * {u, v, θ}
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp
        
        # forces[0] = lateral shear at top of panel (part of segment force)
        # forces[1] = axial force in panel
        # forces[2] = moment at top of panel (should be 0 for cantilever? No, top is free)
        # Wait: the flexibility matrix is for a cantilever fixed at base, free at top.
        # The forces at the top are: shear V, axial P, moment M.
        # For a cantilever with top displacements u,v,θ: 
        # V = (1/fuu)*u - (fuθ/fuu_fθθ - fuθ^2)*θ ... better to use stiffness matrix directly.
        # The stiffness matrix relates top forces to top displacements.
        # forces[0] = shear at top, forces[1] = axial, forces[2] = moment at top.
        # Base moment = - (M_top + V * h) (sign convention)
        # Base axial = axial force (constant along height)
        
        V_top = forces[0]
        P_axial = forces[1]
        M_top = forces[2]
        
        # Base moment (fixed at foundation)
        M_base = -(M_top + V_top * h)  # kip-in
        
        panel_base_moments.append(M_base)
        panel_axial_forces.append(P_axial)
    
    # Joint shears: from connector spring forces
    for i in range(n_joints):
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        v_ip1 = U[1+2*(i+1)]
        θ_ip1 = U[2+2*(i+1)]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2.0) - (v_ip1 - θ_ip1 * L_ip1/2.0)
        V_joint = k_joint[i] * slip  # kip
        joint_shears.append(V_joint)
    
    # Normalize by segment force (which is 1 kip)
    joint_shear_factors = [v for v in joint_shears]  # per kip of segment force
    panel_base_moment_factors = [m for m in panel_base_moments]  # kip-in per kip
    panel_axial_factors = [p for p in panel_axial_forces]  # kip per kip
    
    return k_seg, joint_shear_factors, panel_base_moment_factors, panel_axial_factors

def compute_piers(wall, openings, panels):
    """
    Compute as-built piers (solid wall segments between openings) for a wall.
    Returns list of piers, each with: start, length, panels (list of (panel_id, width)),

    piers = []
    prev_end = 0.0
    panel_idx = 0
    panels_list = panels[wall]
    
    for o_start, o_end, oid in opening_intervals:
        if o_start > prev_end:
            pier_length = o_start - prev_end
            # Assign panels to this pier by accumulating panel widths
            pier_panels = []
            accumulated = 0.0
            while panel_idx < len(panels_list) and accumulated < pier_length - 1e-6:
                pid, pwidth = panels_list[panel_idx]
                if accumulated + pwidth <= pier_length + 1e-6:
                    pier_panels.append((pid, pwidth))
                    accumulated += pwidth
                    panel_idx += 1
                else:

                    remaining = pier_length - accumulated
                    if remaining > 0.1:

                    accumulated = pier_length

    h = WALL_HEIGHT_TO_DECK * 12.0  # in (28 ft = 336 in)
    
    # Panel properties (per panel, not per ft)
    panels = pier['panels']
    n_panels = len(panels)
    if n_panels == 0:
        return 0.0, [], [], []
    
    # Compute panel flexural and shear rigidities
    # For in-plane bending, panel cross-section: thickness = 8 in, width = panel_length (horizontal)
    # Ig = t * b^3 / 12 where t=8 in, b = pwidth_ft * 12 in
    # Icr = 0.5 * Ig (cracked, ACI 318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a))
    # Ag = t * b = 8 * (pwidth_ft * 12) = 96 * pwidth_ft in2
    # Av = 5/6 * Ag = 80 * pwidth_ft in2
    # Ec = 57000 * sqrt(f'c) psi = 4415 ksi
    # Gc = Ec / 2.4 = 1839.6 ksi
    
    panel_fuu = []
    panel_fuθ = []
    panel_fθθ = []
    panel_kvv = []
    panel_lengths = []  # ft
    
    for pid, pwidth in panels:
        # Panel cross-section for in-plane bending
        b_in = pwidth * 12.0  # panel width in inches (horizontal dimension)
        t_in = 8.0  # panel thickness in inches
        
        Ig = t_in * b_in**3 / 12.0  # in4
        Icr = 0.5 * Ig  # cracked moment of inertia
        Ag = t_in * b_in  # in2
        Av = (5.0/6.0) * Ag  # shear area
        
        EI = EC * Icr  # kip-in2 (EC in ksi = kip/in2)
        GA_v = GC * Av  # kip
        EA = EC * Ag  # kip
        
        fuu = h**3 / (3.0 * EI) + h / GA_v
        fuθ = h**2 / (2.0 * EI)
        fθθ = h / EI
        kvv = EA / h
        
        panel_fuu.append(fuu)
        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)
    
    # Joint connector springs
    n_joints = pier['num_joints']
    if connector_mark == 'JC0' or connectors_per_joint == 0:
        k_joint = [0.0] * n_joints
    else:
        k_conn = JOINT_CONNECTORS[connector_mark]['k']  # kip/in per connector
        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints
    
    # Condense segment on common lateral displacement (chord ties panel tops)
    # DAP-2: "The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement.
    # Condensing the segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness k_seg;
    # recovering the internal state for a unit segment force gives the shear in every joint
    # and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force."
    
    # Build flexibility matrix for the segment
    # DOFs per panel: u_i (lateral), v_i (vertical), θ_i (rotation)
    # But chord constrains all u_i = u_seg (common lateral displacement)
    # So we have 1 + 2*n_panels DOFs: u_seg, v_1, θ_1, v_2, θ_2, ...
    
    # Actually, DAP-2 says: "A segment interrupted over part of its height by an opening that does not reach
    # the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are factored
    # by the solid fraction of the height." Our piers are full-height (no spandrels in piers, openings are full height).
    
    # For a unit segment force (1 kip lateral at top), we solve for displacements.
    # The segment force is distributed to panels proportional to their lateral stiffness contribution.
    # But with joint connectors, there's coupling.
    
    # Simplified approach matching DAP-2 verification example:
    # The verification example: 40 ft segment, 4 panels of 10 ft each, h=28 ft, 3xRPC-40 per joint (k=960 kip/in)
    # Result: k_seg = 1279.4 kip/in
    # Without connectors: k_seg = 769.2 kip/in
    
    # Let me implement the full condensation.
    # DOFs: u (common), v1, θ1, v2, θ2, ..., vn, θn
    n_dof = 1 + 2 * n_panels
    K = np.zeros((n_dof, n_dof))
    F = np.zeros(n_dof)
    F[0] = 1.0  # unit lateral force at segment level
    
    # Panel contributions to stiffness matrix
    # For each panel i, local DOFs: u_i (index 0), v_i (index 1+2*i), θ_i (index 2+2*i)
    # But u_i = u_seg (index 0), so panel lateral force goes to DOF 0.
    # Panel flexibility matrix (3x3) for [u, v, θ]:
    # [fuu, 0,   fuθ]
    # [0,   1/kvv, 0]
    # [fuθ, 0,   fθθ]
    # Invert to get stiffness, then assemble.
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        
        # Panel flexibility submatrix
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        
        # Map to global DOFs: u_seg=0, v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i
        dofs = [0, 1+2*i, 2+2*i]
        for r in range(3):
            for c in range(3):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k_panel[r, c]
    
    # Joint connector springs: act on relative vertical slip
    # slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2) - (v_{i+1} - θ_{i+1} * L_{i+1}/2)
    # This is a spring between v_i, θ_i and v_{i+1}, θ_{i+1}
    for i in range(n_joints):
        k = k_joint[i]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0  # in
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        
        # DOFs: v_i=1+2*i, θ_i=2+2*i, v_{i+1}=1+2*(i+1), θ_{i+1}=2+2*(i+1)
        # slip = v_i + θ_i*L_i/2 - v_{i+1} + θ_{i+1}*L_{i+1}/2
        # Energy = 0.5 * k * slip^2
        # Stiffness matrix contributions:
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    # Solve for displacements
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        # Singular - add small regularization
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]
    k_seg = 1.0 / u_seg if abs(u_seg) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    
    # Recover internal forces for unit segment force
    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []

        u_i = U[0]
        v_i = U[1+2*i]
        θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        
        # Panel forces from displacements
        # {F} = [k_panel] * {u, v, θ}
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]
        fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]
        fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]
        kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([
            [fuu, 0.0, fuθ],
            [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0],
            [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]
        ])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp

        # Base axial = axial force (constant along height)

def compute_segment_stiffness(pier, connector_mark, connectors_per_joint):
    h = WALL_HEIGHT_TO_DECK * 12.0  # in
    panels = pier['panels']

        t_in = 8.0
        Ig = t_in * b_in**3 / 12.0
        Icr = 0.5 * Ig
        Ag = t_in * b_in
        Av = (5.0/6.0) * Ag
        EI = EC * Icr
        GA_v = GC * Av
        EA = EC * Ag
        fuu = h**3 / (3.0 * EI) + h / GA_v
        fuθ = h**2 / (2.0 * EI)
        fθθ = h / EI
        kvv = EA / h
        panel_fuu.append(fuu)
        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)
    
    n_joints = pier['num_joints']

    else:

        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints
    
    n_dof = 1 + 2 * n_panels
    K = np.zeros((n_dof, n_dof))
    F = np.zeros(n_dof)
    F[0] = 1.0
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]; fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]; fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]; kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([[fuu, 0.0, fuθ], [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0], [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        dofs = [0, 1+2*i, 2+2*i]
        for r in range(3):
            for c in range(3):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k_panel[r, c]
    
    for i in range(n_joints):
        k = k_joint[i]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]

    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []
    
    for i in range(n_panels):

        fuu = panel_fuu[i]; fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]; fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]; kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([[fuu, 0.0, fuθ], [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0], [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp
        V_top = forces[0]; P_axial = forces[1]; M_top = forces[2]

        panel_base_moments.append(M_base)

        V_joint = k_joint[i] * slip
        joint_shears.append(V_joint)

def compute_segment_stiffness(pier, connector_mark, connectors_per_joint):
    h = WALL_HEIGHT_TO_DECK * 12.0  # in
    panels = pier['panels']
    n_panels = len(panels)
    if n_panels == 0:
        return 0.0, [], [], []
    
    panel_fuu = []
    panel_fuθ = []
    panel_fθθ = []
    panel_kvv = []
    panel_lengths = []
    
    for pid, pwidth in panels:
        b_in = pwidth * 12.0
        t_in = 8.0
        Ig = t_in * b_in**3 / 12.0
        Icr = 0.5 * Ig
        Ag = t_in * b_in
        Av = (5.0/6.0) * Ag
        EI = EC * Icr
        GA_v = GC * Av
        EA = EC * Ag
        fuu = h**3 / (3.0 * EI) + h / GA_v
        fuθ = h**2 / (2.0 * EI)
        fθθ = h / EI
        kvv = EA / h
        panel_fuu.append(fuu)
        panel_fuθ.append(fuθ)
        panel_fθθ.append(fθθ)
        panel_kvv.append(kvv)
        panel_lengths.append(pwidth)
    
    n_joints = pier['num_joints']
    if connector_mark == 'JC0' or connectors_per_joint == 0:
        k_joint = [0.0] * n_joints
    else:
        k_conn = JOINT_CONNECTORS[connector_mark]['k']
        k_joint = [connectors_per_joint * k_conn] * n_joints
    
    n_dof = 1 + 2 * n_panels
    K = np.zeros((n_dof, n_dof))
    F = np.zeros(n_dof)
    F[0] = 1.0
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]; fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]; fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]; kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([[fuu, 0.0, fuθ], [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0], [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        dofs = [0, 1+2*i, 2+2*i]
        for r in range(3):
            for c in range(3):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k_panel[r, c]
    
    for i in range(n_joints):
        k = k_joint[i]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0
        L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        dofs = [1+2*i, 2+2*i, 1+2*(i+1), 2+2*(i+1)]
        coeffs = [1.0, L_i/2.0, -1.0, L_ip1/2.0]
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                K[dofs[r], dofs[c]] += k * coeffs[r] * coeffs[c]
    
    try:
        U = np.linalg.solve(K, F)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        K_reg = K + np.eye(n_dof) * 1e-12
        U = np.linalg.solve(K_reg, F)
    
    u_seg = U[0]
    k_seg = 1.0 / u_seg if abs(u_seg) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    
    joint_shears = []
    panel_base_moments = []
    panel_axial_forces = []
    
    for i in range(n_panels):
        u_i = U[0]; v_i = U[1+2*i]; θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        fuu = panel_fuu[i]; fuθ = panel_fuθ[i]; fθθ = panel_fθθ[i]; kvv = panel_kvv[i]
        f_panel = np.array([[fuu, 0.0, fuθ], [0.0, 1.0/kvv, 0.0], [fuθ, 0.0, fθθ]])
        k_panel = np.linalg.inv(f_panel)
        disp = np.array([u_i, v_i, θ_i])
        forces = k_panel @ disp
        V_top = forces[0]; P_axial = forces[1]; M_top = forces[2]
        M_base = -(M_top + V_top * h)
        panel_base_moments.append(M_base)
        panel_axial_forces.append(P_axial)
    
    for i in range(n_joints):
        v_i = U[1+2*i]; θ_i = U[2+2*i]
        v_ip1 = U[1+2*(i+1)]; θ_ip1 = U[2+2*(i+1)]
        L_i = panel_lengths[i] * 12.0; L_ip1 = panel_lengths[i+1] * 12.0
        slip = (v_i + θ_i * L_i/2.0) - (v_ip1 - θ_ip1 * L_ip1/2.0)
        V_joint = k_joint[i] * slip
        joint_shears.append(V_joint)
    
    return k_seg, joint_shears, panel_base_moments, panel_axial_forces
